key.name: swap-windows
key.summary: Swap all windows between the top and bottom screen
key.description: F8 (screen arrows) on the Zenbook Duo keyboard sends XF86Launch2.

key.name: move-window-to-other-screen
key.summary: Move the focused window to the other screen

key.name: display-controls
key.description: Extra shortcuts for the display controls. F7 (the projection key) sends Super+P, which display-controls-on-super-p takes over.

key.name: main-display-switch
key.summary: Ask which screen becomes the main display
key.description: Shift+F7: a bubble on every screen; "Make this the main display" on one of them makes that screen the main display. The keyboard drops Shift and sends Super+P for Shift+F7; the Zenbook Duo services recognise that and call ShiftF7Pressed. Shift+Super+P is the fallback.

key.name: five-finger-main-display
key.summary: Five fingers held on a screen open the main-display switch
key.description: Holding five fingers still on one touch screen for a moment shows the same bubble as Shift+F7.

key.name: display-controls-on-super-p
key.summary: Open the display controls with Super+P too
key.description: Detached, F7 sends Super+P, which GNOME uses for its display switcher; this opens the display controls instead.

key.name: touch-keyboard
key.summary: Show the on-screen keyboard when a text field is tapped with a finger
key.description: GNOME normally only does this without a physical keyboard; clicking with the touchpad or mouse still never opens it.

key.name: keyboard-on-other-screen
key.summary: Keep the on-screen keyboard on the bottom screen
key.description: With both screens on, the on-screen keyboard appears on the bottom screen, or on the top screen when it would cover a text field on the bottom screen, and the swipe-up gesture only works from the bottom screen's edge.
